title: Paranormal investigator Colin Browen reveals signs your house might be haunted ahead of Halloween
excerpt: EXCLUSIVE: Famous paranormal investigator Colin Browen gave his professional insight on common signs a home is haunted and the special equipment used to track them down
content:
As spooky season is upon us, famous paranormal investigator Colin Browen shared his insight on the haunted houses and the common patterns he's encountered in his career.

Colin is one of the most sought-after paranormal investigators and filmmakers. He’s the creator of The Paranormal Files (featuring over 500 million views) and the co-host of the hit true crime podcast Murder in America.

Colin has dedicated many years to investigating dark spaces across the world, including reportedly haunted homes, hospitals, prisons, hotels, and historic landmarks — and through this unveiled the truth behind the unexplained.

One of the focuses of his career has been exploring allegedly haunted houses, which has led him to identify some commonalities and telltale signs that your home could be experiencing paranormal activity. This comes as one paranormal influencer died after destroying a "cursed" statue to test how long she could live.

In an interview with The Mirror US, Colin shared his advice to someone who has an inkling that their house could be haunted.

He explained, "Well, most of the time, things that we believe might be paranormal have rational explanations. We experience this all the time during our paranormal investigations — most of the time, the things that go bump in the night are really outdated air conditioning systems or rodents in the walls."

"However, it's the 1% of paranormal experiences and reports that are completely inexplicable, that defy all rational explanation, that fascinate me," he continued. "If you believe your house is haunted, I recommend that you try first, before seeking any sort of paranormal treatment, to attempt to debunk what you are seeing or experiencing."

Colin said unusual noises are the most frequently reported signs people note in allegedly haunted houses.

"I can't tell you how many people have shared stories with me over the last decade about the things that they've experienced in their own homes, and, most of the time, these stories revolve around noises that they hear — voices coming from other rooms, knocking in the walls, or footsteps from upper floors — and, having lived in a haunted house myself, I understand how frightening those experiences can be," Colin said.

The paranormal investigator added that other common reports include electrical disturbances, lightbulbs burning out in front of people's eyes, and shadow figures. He said that, with these figures, people claim to see them out of the corners of their eyes and feel their presence at the corners of their rooms.

Once rational explanations have been ruled out, that's when Colin and his team step in. Colin said that they use all sorts of tools like ITC devices, like Spirit Boxes or Ovilus devices, EMF meters, REM pods, voice recorders and SLS cameras, among others.

"You could spend $20,000 building out the best paranormal toolbox imaginable, with every sort of device possible — but, at the end of the day, I think that the best paranormal investigation device is ourselves — the human body," he said. "In order to really understand the paranormal, we have to understand how it affects us and each one of our senses. If you feel like something is wrong, usually, something is wrong — and you should always listen to your intuition, especially if you believe that you're experiencing a haunting."

Colin continued, "I've found that some of the best paranormal evidence that I've ever captured or experienced has come from the environment and my body itself — phantom smells, tingling sensations, cool breezes, and feelings or thoughts that have popped into my head completely unprovoked."

The paranormal expert went on to note that although their equipment can provide them with some evidence, it does not give them concrete answers. He explained that the information they gather through these investigations is like "pieces of an incomplete puzzle" that will "never truly" be solved. He added that all of this technology is experimental.

Colin also explained that the first thing that paranormal investigators look for is the environmental conditions that might be causing a haunting. He shared that one of the first things they do when entering a home is to check for "elevated levels of EMF" (electromagnetic field) in environments.

He went on to note that the biggest factor in hauntings is the history of the property. He explained that if there isn't any tragic history or deaths connected to a residence, it is unlikely a spirit is haunting the home.

The biggest misconception about haunted homes, from Colin's perspective, is that they're all "evil" or "frightening," he said. "I've investigated dozens of homes and places that were filled with happy, jovial spirits — in fact, one night, we spent the entire night telling jokes to the spirits and watched as they played with our devices and seemingly laughed along with us."

He continued, "In horror movies and documentaries about the paranormal world, usually hauntings are portrayed as intense, frightening and disturbing; however, in real life, it's never black and white. Although it's possible you may run into something more on the negative side, and you may not be dealing with Casper, most of the time, the spirits we encounter and interact with seem to be lost souls, in a way — not angry, demonic beings intent on raising hell — simply energies and spiritual entities that we don't really understand."

Due to this, Colin emphasized that even if your house is haunted, the majority of the time, the spirits are not interested in hurting you. He explained that, in most cases, these spirits are just trying to be acknowledged, and other times they are requesting to "be acknowledged" or "helped with a task or given some form of respect."
